Guides › The pare command

The pare command

pare turns .ts files into .js files by erasing the types. It does nothing else: no bundling, no minifying, no type checking, no Node packages.

Commands

Command What it does
pare src Writes each src/**/*.ts as .js next to its source. .mts becomes .mjs, .cts becomes .cjs.
pare src --outdir js Writes under js/ instead, keeping the folder structure below src/. The base is the input folder itself, so src/pages/home.ts becomes js/pages/home.js.
pare src --check-only Reports errors and writes nothing. Use it in CI or a pre-commit hook.
pare --stdin < in.ts > out.js Reads one file from stdin and writes JavaScript to stdout. For editors and pipelines.
pare --version Prints the version.

Inputs can be files, folders (searched recursively) or globs (*, ?, **) for shells that do not expand them. .d.ts files and node_modules are skipped. A symlink or junction back to a folder already searched is skipped. The server and share of a UNC pattern (\\srv\share) must be written out, with no wildcard.

An existing foo.js next to foo.ts is replaced, like tsc and esbuild do. Keep hand-written JavaScript out of the source folders, or use --outdir.

bash 
$ cat in.ts
const n: number = 1 as const;
$ pare --stdin < in.ts
const n         = 1         ;

Relative imports

Browsers and Node load .js files, so Pare rewrites relative specifiers that name a TypeScript file: ./util.ts becomes ./util.js, .mts becomes .mjs, .cts becomes .cjs. This covers import, export ... from and import("...").

Exit codes

Code Meaning
0 Every file was stripped (or checked).
1 A file uses syntax that cannot be erased. That file gets no output; the message names the line.
2 I/O or usage error, for example a missing input.
bash 
$ pare --check-only bad.ts
bad.ts:1:1: error PARE100: 'enum' generates runtime code and cannot be erased (use a 'const' object with 'as const' instead of 'enum')
$ pare missing.ts
pare: missing.ts: no such file or directory

Every rejection in a run is reported, not only the first.

Strip again on every save

pare has no watch mode. Let Node or Deno watch the folder and run it. The sample has a small script, samples/CliSite/watch.mjs, that runs pare once and prints errors without stopping:

bash 
node --watch-path=samples/CliSite/src samples/CliSite/watch.mjs
deno run --watch=samples/CliSite/src --allow-run=pare --allow-env samples/CliSite/watch.mjs

Copy the script into your project and change the paths.

In CI

bash 
pare src --check-only

fails the job with exit code 1 if any file uses syntax Pare cannot erase. To also check types, run tsc --noEmit after it; see Type checking in CI.

Install options

dotnet tool install -g Extrode.Pare.Cli installs one framework-dependent tool for every platform. It needs the .NET 10 runtime and starts slower than the NativeAOT binary. The NativeAOT binaries for osx-arm64, osx-x64, linux-arm64, linux-x64, linux-musl-arm64, linux-musl-x64, win-x64 and win-arm64 come as archives on the releases page and need no .NET.
